implementation_notes: scala.Function1 is the standard library's unary function type and carries both combinators as concrete methods: `f andThen g` applies f first, `f compose g` applies g first, each returning a new Function1 (scala-lang.org API); `Function.chain(Seq(f, g))` composes an ordered list, and eta-expansion (`method _`) or a partially applied function supplies the steps. Nothing needs building, so the pattern is fully native, and the only adaptation left is arity: Function2 and above must be tupled or curried before they can join a chain.
code_sketch:
val normalize: String => String = _.trim.toLowerCase
val digest:    String => String = s => sha256Hex(s)

val normalizeThenDigest: String => String = normalize andThen digest
// equivalent: Function.chain(Seq(normalize, digest))
val hash = normalizeThenDigest(raw)
pitfalls: andThen/compose exist on Function1 only: a Function2 needs tupling or currying first, and a method needs `_` eta-expansion to become a value.
compose applies right-to-left while andThen applies left-to-right; chains that mix both are a documented source of ordering bugs.
Function.chain takes a homogeneous Seq[A => A], so chains that change type at every step cannot use it and must nest andThen instead.
